client_brief:
Coastal destination imagery for the quieter season

Cape Marren's campaign runs October to April. We need a welcoming coastal image set, but not sunshine or sea conditions that misrepresent that season. Six members have contributed photographs; suitable licensed coastal imagery can fill the declared context role.

Final handoff

 Shoulder-season destination poster: 1 named export. Cape Marren is identified. Stock coastal imagery is not labelled as a named member venue.

 Destination itinerary carousel: 6 named exports. Stops use the approved member names. The sequence supports a plausible visitor itinerary.

 Tourism member feature: 1 named export. The featured member is identified accurately. The imagery corresponds to that member or is explicitly illustrative.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Regional destination marketing, an alliance of independent coastal member businesses
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A visitor alliance of twenty two independent member businesses along the Cape Marren coast on the North American Atlantic seaboard. Coordinated by Nell on behalf of the members. Small, member funded, regional in reach.
brand_identity.about: Cape Marren Coast Alliance markets a stretch of independent coast to shoulder season visitors. Summer sells itself; the work is October to April, when a harbour seafood room, a cider barn, a point light, a bookshop, a bakery and an oyster landing either make a living or do not. The campaign has to feel like that season honestly: warm low sun, weather, wool, wet stone, a lit window at four in the afternoon, quiet compositions with one or two people. Members have to see themselves in it, because members who cannot see themselves do not renew.
brand_identity.audience: Travellers aged 30 to 60, driving from within four hours, mostly couples and pairs of friends rather than families. They spend 200 to 600 dollars per party across a two or three night shoulder season weekend on rooms, meals, cider and a walk.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid range and real. Positioned above a peak summer holiday treatment (which would oversell blue water and hard sun) and below a 1,500 dollar luxury coastal weekend (which would go near monochrome and strand the bakery and the cider barn). Editorial rather than promotional, and never promising a season the coast cannot deliver in November.
brand_identity.typography: Newzald (serif), Book weight, sets headlines: 180 pt on the destination poster, 64 px on each carousel page, 42 pt on the member feature. Atlas Grotesk (sans), Regular, carries captions, member names, trail numbers and opening months at 11 pt in print and 28 px on screen, with body running 10.5 pt on 15 pt. Opening months use Atlas Grotesk Medium tabular figures so they align down a column. Never set a member name in the serif, and never letterspace the headline.
brand_identity.voice: Grounded and truthful. Warm about the place without overselling it, and specific about what a visitor will actually find when they arrive out of season.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No written brand guidelines exist. The only brand file on hand is the alliance mark left by the previous agency, supplied as a single vector file with nothing else: no color system, no type list and no usage notes. Members submit their own photographs and object shots, and the campaign look is set by this brief rather than by any existing kit.
brand_identity.values: Honesty about the season, keeping every member visible, and supporting the independent businesses that fund the alliance.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

assets.description: Original compass geometry with transparent canvas, viewBox and outlined Georgia lettering. No font dependency.
1200 x 1200 transparent raster companion to the outlined master.
